title: Gradient-Domain ReSTIR Path Tracing
reading_extent: Publisher full-text HTML: Sections 4–6; direct PDF exceeded web size limit.
locator: Sections 4.1–4.4, 5 Results, 6 Discussion and Conclusion; Figures 9–12
mechanism: Resample paired-pixel paths directly in gradient space, with adaptive edge-aligned spatial reuse and positive/negative reservoirs to reduce sign noise; reconstruct using a separate primal Area ReSTIR image.
reported_context: Falcor, RTX 5090, Ryzen 5900X, 1920×1080 moving camera. L2 Poisson reconstruction costs 11 ms; L1 costs 300 ms. L2 cost is included in equal-time comparisons.
caveats: Assumes affine object transforms. High-frequency temporal turbulence remains without temporal gradients; reconstruction is an additional cost. Neural reconstruction efficiency is prospective, not demonstrated as a DLSS integration.
relevance: RTXPT research branch: separate gradient reservoirs, primal pass and reconstruction interface. RTXDI core can supply path shifts but cannot obtain this by merely changing a spatial-neighbor picker.
rationale: Promising detail preservation, but a separate estimator/reconstruction architecture follows the seven requested sampling priorities.
validation: Compare paired-pixel reuse against gradient-after-ReSTIR at equal complete frame time; measure signed-gradient error, reconstructed error, deformation failures and temporal instability.

title: Reservoir Splatting for Temporal Path Resampling and Motion Blur
reading_extent: Author abstract, official repository README and indexed supplemental Section 1–3 excerpt; large main PDF could not be opened.
locator: Abstract; supplemental Sections 1–3; repository Temporal Resampling Options
mechanism: Forward-project exact prior-frame primary hits rather than only backprojecting current pixels. Combine splats and backup gather samples using MIS. Multiple time splats extend reuse to motion blur; depth of field is also supported.
reported_context: Author abstract reports better resampling quality than Area ReSTIR at up to 10% lower cost; this is not a measured RTXDI_Next result.
caveats: Forward scatter requires deterministic handling of collisions and uncovered pixels; multi-splat partitions raise storage. Repository describes a Falcor 8 prototype, not an RTXDI API port.
relevance: RTXPT temporal candidate-production pass plus RTXDI PT-compatible sample/weight import. Foundational dependency for the 2026 multi-layer splatting branch.
rationale: Establish a single-layer splat plus backup baseline before adding hidden-surface layers.
validation: Separate gather-only, scatter-only and scatter-plus-backup; test subpixel moving geometry, lens aperture, camera cuts, splat overflow, shutter support and unbiased mean.

title: Unbiased Differential Visibility Using Fixed-Step Walk-on-Spherical-Caps And Closest Silhouettes
reading_extent: Author abstract and indexed first-page PDF abstract/Figure 1; full PDF size blocked web extraction.
mechanism: Construct a velocity field for warped-area differential visibility using fixed-step walks on spherical caps and cone queries for closest silhouettes.
reported_context: A differentiable-rendering visibility derivative estimator, not a primal-lighting or temporal-reuse result.
caveats: The fixed-step field is continuous but need not be harmonic. Requires silhouette-oriented geometric queries; existing primal ray tracing alone is insufficient.
relevance: An optional differentiable/inverse-rendering RTXPT extension; no direct replacement for RTXDI visibility tests.
rationale: The current goal is forward rendering quality/performance, so derivative estimation has no immediate acceptance target.
validation: If adopted later, compare geometry derivatives to finite differences and test silhouette discontinuities, not just rendered color.

title: Many-Light Rendering Using ReSTIR-Sampled Shadow Maps
reading_extent: Publisher full-text Section 3, plus author abstract; direct PDF too large.
locator: Sections 3.1 Selecting Lights, 3.2 Practical Algorithm, 3.3 Maintaining Temporal Stability
mechanism: Use a ranking reservoir process to select a budgeted subset of full-resolution light shadow maps, with imperfect shadow maps elsewhere; a separate shading reservoir process evaluates lighting. Variance-based hysteresis stabilizes upgrades and downgrades.
caveats: Two reservoirs prevent ranking/shading feedback flicker; combining them degrades stability or noise. Imperfect maps approximate visibility, so this is not exact ray-traced visibility.
relevance: A separate low-end/raster RTXDI sample backend, or an importance-ranking experiment. Not a baseline visibility replacement for RTXPT.
rationale: Avoid mixing visibility approximation into evaluation of unbiased PT resampling improvements.
validation: If adopted, measure map generation cost, memory, ranking flicker, approximation error and temporal response separately from reservoir estimator error.

title: Area ReSTIR: Resampling for Real-time Defocus and Antialiasing
reading_extent: Author project abstract and indexed paper Sections 4.1–4.6 excerpts; complete large PDF unavailable in web extraction.
locator: Sections 4.1 Area Reservoirs, 4.3 Temporal Reuse, 4.4 General Pixel Filters, 4.6 Depth of Field
mechanism: Include film and lens coordinates in the reservoir domain. Fractional-pixel temporal tracking and camera-aware shifts improve reuse of subpixel detail and defocus. The robust option can borrow shifted samples from four overlapping prior reservoirs.
reported_context: Supports antialiasing and depth of field; basis for later splatting and gradient-domain work.
caveats: Aperture support and shift Jacobians matter; primary-hit reconnection can leave the aperture. General filters alter overlap/MIS weights. The author repository publishes only the DI implementation, modifies scene-history storage outside its module, and warns module-only copying produces bias/errors; noisy camera-domain G-buffers challenge denoisers.
relevance: Extend RTXPT camera/sample domain and RTXDI PT history metadata before camera effects or splatting. Audit what current RTXDI already implements first.
rationale: Use as domain-correctness reference and comparison baseline for the requested 2026 temporal techniques.
validation: Pinhole and large aperture, subpixel wires/fur, fractional motion, box/non-box pixel filters, aperture-boundary failure, long-run mean.

title: Decorrelating ReSTIR Samplers via MCMC Mutations
reading_extent: Publisher full-text method Section 3 and limitations Section 7; indexed paper excerpts.
locator: Section 3 Method, Equation 16, Algorithm 3, Section 7 Limitations; Figures 12–13
mechanism: Mutate selected reservoir samples using Metropolis–Hastings, usually after temporal reuse; update the contribution weight by the old/new target-function ratio before further resampling.
reported_context: Demonstrated in DI and PT; mutations address correlation and duplicate-sample impoverishment.
caveats: Non-negligible runtime; can improve perceptual correlation without lowering MSE. It is not a discovery mechanism for missing important transport, and even unlimited mutations need not remove all correlations.
relevance: Optional RTXDI DI/PT decorrelation stage, especially when long temporal history is valuable. Compare to compatible-neighbor selection rather than assuming gains add.
rationale: Revisit if improved neighbors and PT++ still leave visible boiling/blotches.
validation: Measure covariance/FLIP and denoised sequences alongside MSE, complete frame cost and target-ratio boundary handling.

title: Conditional Resampled Importance Sampling and ReSTIR
reading_extent: Author-affiliated archival abstract, indexed first-page paper excerpt, official prototype README.
locator: Abstract and Figure 1; official prototype Introduction
mechanism: Extend GRIS to conditional domains with correct joint contribution weights; a final gather reuses path suffixes after one or more unreused prefix bounces.
reported_context: A proof-of-concept with reduced blotchy correlation and improved denoiser behavior; prototype is explicitly unoptimized.
caveats: Conditional independence and contribution-weight requirements must be preserved. Suffix reuse cannot silently inherit full-path reservoir weights.
relevance: Theoretical reference for RTXPT suffix-guiding/conditional reuse and PG interactions; not needed to add all seven focus methods to DI.
rationale: Use when choosing between full-path reuse and a final-gather architecture.
validation: Compare full-path and suffix reuse, denoised correlation, unbiased mean and extra rays at equal time.

title: Amortizing Samples in Physics-Based Inverse Rendering Using ReSTIR
reading_extent: Author project results and indexed paper multi-view Algorithm 8/computational-overhead excerpt.
locator: Project results; paper multi-view estimator and Computational overhead discussion
mechanism: Reuse sampling work across inverse-rendering optimization iterations/views, including gradient estimates and preserved occluded reservoirs.
reported_context: Project reports up to 100× lower gradient relative error and up to 20× lower reconstruction error in its inverse-rendering comparisons, not forward rendering FPS.
caveats: A practical geometry-optimization variant checks visibility only in current geometry and introduces bias; learning rate limits its effect.
relevance: Future material/shape fitting tool around RTXPT, not the forward-rendering fork core.
validation: If adopted, compare optimization error versus complete wall time and geometry-change bias.

title: Generalized Resampled Importance Sampling: Foundations of ReSTIR
reading_extent: Indexed primary PDF abstract/introduction and Sections 3.2, 4.1–4.2; supplement contents, not complete proof review.
locator: Sections 3.2 and 4, Equation 4 partition of unity and Equation 8 unbiased contribution weights; supplement S.1–S.5
mechanism: Formalize resampling of correlated samples with tractable unbiased contribution weights and domain-changing shift maps/Jacobians; under conditions derive convergence and variance guarantees.
reported_context: Establishes the ReSTIR PT framework and its distinction from classical independent-sample RIS.
caveats: Correlation alone does not grant convergence. Correct support, resampling MIS partition and mapping weights are obligations; an arbitrary heuristic can converge to a wrong answer.
relevance: Mandatory estimator contract for every RTXDI PT extension and shared reservoir schema.
rationale: Correctness prerequisite to combining neighbor selection, stochastic MIS, LoD and PG.
validation: Use analytic tiny scenes, independent repetitions, canonical candidates, inverse shifts/Jacobians and partition-of-unity checks.

title: Fast Volume Rendering with Spatiotemporal Reservoir Resampling
reading_extent: Publisher abstract and indexed author-paper first page; PDF open timed out.
mechanism: Extend reuse to volumetric path space, using cheap approximate scattering/transmittance during candidate selection and unbiased final evaluation.
reported_context: Handles dynamic illumination, volumetric emission and multiple scattering; the approximation in selection need not bias final shading if weighting is correct.
caveats: Medium path domains and transmittance estimators differ from surface PT. Figure examples are interactive volumetric results, not a 60 Hz guarantee.
relevance: Separate RTXPT participating-media extension; RTXDI surface reservoirs cannot be assumed compatible.
rationale: Establish robust surface baseline first; medium support has its own path-state contract.
validation: Homogeneous analytic transmittance, heterogeneous media, zero-density transitions, multiple scattering, mean and memory.

title: Rearchitecting Spatiotemporal Resampling for Production
reading_extent: Publisher abstract and indexed primary paper Figure 2 / Sections 5–7 overview.
mechanism: Rework candidate presampling and memory coherence, ray budgets, synchronization, spatial-neighbor choices and separation of shading from reuse for production.
reported_context: Author abstract reports up to 7× lower lighting cost over the earlier research implementation.
caveats: These are historical changes underlying productization, not fresh gains to add on top of current RTXDI. GPU timing must include all new passes and synchronization.
relevance: Mandatory design/performance reference for the fork and integration with RTXPT dispatch scheduling.
rationale: Audit already-shipped work before porting research pseudocode or increasing reservoir traffic.
validation: Profile occupancy, cache/memory transactions, rays, barriers and full-frame time against the pinned upstream baseline.

title: Glossy Probe Reprojection for Interactive Global Illumination
reading_extent: Author project abstract and indexed primary first-page method overview.
mechanism: Precompute directional glossy light probes with adaptive parameterization; gather using path perturbation and split roughness convolution between precomputation and runtime filtering.
reported_context: Interactive walkthroughs for static scenes with opaque objects; diffuse light maps complement glossy probes.
caveats: Baked scene assumptions and probe storage/reprojection limits do not match general dynamic path tracing.
relevance: Alternative cached-lighting branch or scene-class baseline around RTXPT, not a ReSTIR reservoir feature.
rationale: Different architecture and static-scene tradeoff; prioritize dynamic unbiased sampling.
validation: If explored, measure bake time/storage, parallax/occlusion error and stale probes after edits.

title: Spatiotemporal Reservoir Resampling for Real-time Ray Tracing with Dynamic Direct Lighting
reading_extent: Author abstract and indexed primary paper Sections 5–6 evaluation/temporal weighting excerpt.
locator: Abstract; Sections 5–6 reservoir storage, temporal weighting and results
mechanism: Select weighted reservoir light samples and reuse across pixels/frames to spend visibility/shading on high-contribution candidates.
reported_context: The paper distinguishes unbiased and lower-noise biased versions; original results used RTX 2080 Ti/Titan RTX and omit shared G-buffer rasterization costs.
caveats: Energy loss in the biased form and temporal sample dominance are explicit tradeoffs. Old speedup ratios are not expected incremental gains over RTXDI 3.1.
relevance: Foundational DI correctness and baseline reference; RTXDI already supplies its production lineage.
rationale: Keep DI as a separately measurable baseline while modifying PT.
validation: Direct-light analytic scenes, visibility discontinuities, dynamic lights and history limits; report biased options separately.
